Cairn is an Arch Linux ISO with a Hyprland desktop already put together, and an installer that does
the whole install without a network. This is its first release.

**It is early, and the version number is the honest part.** Expect bugs, expect things to change,
and don't put it on a machine whose contents you care about. It has been installed end to end in
QEMU (UEFI, writable disk). It has not yet been run on physical hardware.

## What you get

- A Hyprland session on Wayland with the pieces that make it a desktop: waybar, rofi, mako,
  hyprlock and hypridle, swaybg, Alacritty, Firefox, Nautilus, and SDDM to log in through. Audio is
  PipeWire with WirePlumber. Bluetooth, networking and power profiles are installed *and* enabled.
- One warm dark palette across all of it — including GTK 3, GTK 4 (libadwaita ignores
  `gtk-theme-name` entirely, so its named colors are written directly) and Qt 5/6 through
  qt5ct/qt6ct. Nautilus doesn't glow white in the middle of a dark session.
- Screenshots on Print, working volume and brightness keys, clipboard history on Super+V.

## The install

**No network, at any point.** The finished system is already on the ISO as a compressed image; the
installer extracts it and then does only the per-machine setup, so an install takes a couple of
minutes on a laptop with no wifi driver loaded and no cable in reach. Nvidia's drivers sit in a
side repository on the disc and are installed from there only if you ask for them.

The installer starts on its own when the ISO boots. On a machine with a display it runs in a small
Wayland kiosk so you get truecolor and real icons; on anything else it falls back to the plain
console, swaps the Nerd Font glyphs for CP437 and repaints the console's sixteen colour slots. It's
a wizard with the step list always on screen, and almost everything is pre-filled.

It will **erase one entire disk**: GPT, an ESP, everything else as root, optional LUKS2 on that
root, Btrfs with `@`, `@home`, `@log`, `@cache` and `@snapshots`, an optional swapfile, and
systemd-boot. The review screen makes you type `ERASE` before any of it begins. Every command it
runs, and all of its output, goes to the screen and to `/var/log/cairn-install.log` at once.

## Known limitations

- **x86_64 UEFI only.** The live ISO boots under BIOS, but the installer writes systemd-boot, so
  the installed system needs UEFI. There is no ARM build: archiso cannot produce an aarch64 ISO and
  Arch Linux has no aarch64 repositories.
- **One disk, wiped whole.** No dual-boot, no manual partitioning, no reusing an existing ESP.
- **Nvidia means the open kernel modules** (`nvidia-open`, or the DKMS flavour), so Turing —
  GTX 16 and RTX 20 — and newer. Older cards fall back to nouveau.
- **Nothing is updated during the install**, which is the point of an offline one. Run
  `sudo pacman -Syu` after the first boot.
- **The theme is a one-time bake**, not a theme engine: no switcher, no daemon watching for
  changes. Changing the palette means editing `colors.lua` and the five other config files that
  restate the same hex values in their own syntax.
- **Not tested on physical hardware.** If you try it there, an
  [issue](https://github.com/jaykeraliya0/cairn/issues) saying what broke is the most useful thing
  you can send.

The ISO is about 3.7 GiB, so it wants an 8 GB stick or larger.
